new_findings.location: inputs/candidate/tasks.md T3.1/T7.1 execution rows (83–85), execution order (94), next.py ownership (105), task cards (128–130), and T3.1 completion (146); validation.md g15(b) (140); design.md §7 (222–225) and §10 (380–386)
new_findings.problem: The new g15(b) is a T3.1 completion requirement: compute/use the remaining active budget, time out at that bound, and have next prioritize the expired stop. T3.1 explicitly excludes active-union calculation, while T7.1 owns that calculation and next/safety deadline routing and depends on both T3.1 and T6.1. Consequently the prescribed T3.1 -> T6.1 -> T7.1 order cannot pass the T3.1 completion check within the stated ownership boundaries. No pre-T3.1 remaining-budget/deadline interface, fixture contract, or later integration-test ownership is provided. The explicit dependency column remains acyclic; the new acceptance criterion introduces the backward dependency.
new_findings.basis: The handoff's dispatch-plan contract requires each task to be independently assignable with explicit adjacent interfaces and dependency-satisfied verification. D12 covers required-verification gaps; D13/D47 and retained DUR-08/AC-D17 require the real active-budget/safety behavior. Unlike R15-03's former ambiguous split, the new cards explicitly exclude the needed calculation from T3.1 and assign routing to the later task.
new_findings.expected_fix: Define an earlier owned remaining-budget/deadline seam and test T3.1's local runner against that contract, with the public next/safety integration assertion owned by T7.1; alternatively split/reorder the budget work so its real prerequisite exists before T3.1. Update cards, shared-file ownership, dependencies, matrix ownership, completion conditions and coverage consistently. Preserve real coverage for retained elapsed time, the shorter remaining-budget bound, stop priority and zero new dispatch; do not merely stub the complete public-path assertion or add a reverse edge that creates a cycle.
